prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one text-free chapter miniature, portrait 1024 x 1536, readable when displayed at 96 and 160 pixels wide.
Reference 1 (chapter-01 title) establishes ONLY the precise PinPin identity, story setting, slender golden quill, and warm richly dimensional woodland illustration. Reference 2 (bath miniature) establishes ONLY the tight character-led framing and thumbnail clarity, NOT its setting or extra characters.
Recompose chapter 1 as an intimate, joyous hero portrait at the restored forest lake. Exactly ONE young hedgehog, Mr. PinPin, with the first reference's expressive round cream face, chestnut quills, black nose, round ears, and soft natural fur. PinPin stands on the mossy lake bank holding the same slender golden quill upright in one forepaw, other forepaw relaxed against his chest. His delighted face and large distinct quill are the clear visual focus. Keep two coherent forelimbs and two small grounded hindfeet, no duplicated paws. PinPin looks toward the raised quill with quiet wonder.
Move the camera close: PinPin occupies about three quarters of the picture height and most of its width, his large face in the upper middle; the top of his quills near the top edge with a comfortable margin. Keep the golden quill clearly silhouetted against softly contrasting blue-green water beside his face; enough shaft and broad feather surface to read as the story's fine golden quill, not a wand or brush. No blank sky for lettering. A simple visible crescent of luminous lake water on the right, a few broad lily pads with one white lily, softly simplified distant evergreen forest, a few soft willow fronds along the top edge give clear location. Narrow mossy bank grounds him at the bottom. Reduce busy foreground sticks, little flowers, stones and foliage. Soft quiet low-contrast background, stronger cream-face and chestnut-quill silhouettes, nuanced natural daylight with warm rim lighting. Preserve the same detailed tactile fur, quills, moss and luminous water, dimensional cinematic children's-book style; not a flat cartoon, vector icon or shiny plastic toy.
Absolutely no text, lettering, captions, numbers, logos or watermark. Do not add Mama, baby, rabbit, other animals, clothes or cottage. This is a fresh tighter composition of the established lake-and-golden-quill cover, not just removing title text. Output one complete finished portrait.
